explanations: hashKey wraps to a signed 32-bit integer (`| 0`), so for longer keys the hash is often negative. In JavaScript, % keeps the sign of the left operand, so -7 % 4 is -3, and this.shards[-3] is undefined. Reinterpreting the hash as unsigned (`>>> 0`) before the modulo always gives 0..n-1. Keys whose hash was already non-negative (every short ID that used to work) keep the same shard, so no existing data moves.
